officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.file()/Bun.write() remain the recommended optimized file APIs, and node:fs is explicitly sanctioned for what they do not cover (mkdir, readdir). No deprecations or breaking changes affect the read/write shapes this PRD needs: BunFile.text(), Bun.write(path, string), and node:fs readFileSync/writeFileSync are all current.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: Official docs recommend the async Bun.file/Bun.write pair, while the local curated invariant deliberately keeps synchronous point-reads (readFileSync/existsSync/appendFileSync) on node:fs so callers and in-memory test collectors are not forced async; the derivation and artifact-writer call sites here are synchronous, so the local convention wins and the implementer must not migrate them to Bun.file.

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/commands/stats.ts:191]: `cam stats cycles --rebuild` surfaces a raw uncaught ENOENT stack trace instead of the project's clear-message error convention when `scripts/cam/` does not exist. `defaultWriteArtifact` calls `writeFileSync(join(cwd, ...CYCLE_METRICS_ARTIFACT_REL_PATH), ...)` with no guard and no try/catch, so the throw escapes `runStatsCycles` (called at stats.ts:238) and escapes dispatchStats. Reproduced by the reviewer in a temp dir containing only `.claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl`: exit code is 1 (correct) but the operator sees `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl'` plus a `at runStatsCycles (src/commands/stats.ts:238:74)` stack frame and a `Bun v1.3.13 (macOS arm64)` footer. This is asymmetric with the sibling read path, which handles the exact same missing-artifact class gracefully (`bun index.ts stats cycles` exits 0 with 'No cycle data recorded yet'), and with the file's own module-header contract ('always exits 0 -- a missing or empty event log is "no data yet", not an error'). `printError` from '../logging/color.ts' is the established convention for precisely this absent-artifact case (see src/commands/suggestions.ts:170). Fix mechanically in one file: wrap the `writeArtifact` call at stats.ts:236-239 in a try/catch that emits `printError` with the resolved path plus a remediation hint and returns a non-zero code, or mkdir -p the parent directory before writing.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/commands/stats.ts:148]: `renderCyclesTable` pads cycleId with `padEnd(CYCLE_COL_WIDTH = 42)` and never truncates, but cycleId is an OPAQUE free-form string (branch names) that reaches 47 chars in the committed artifact. The Cycle and Issue columns therefore collide on real data today, e.g. `cam/CAM-94-blocked-narration-supervisor-outcomeCAM-94` and `cam/CAM-134-remove-dead-buildmergedescriptionCAM-134`, in `bun index.ts stats cycles`. This is the same separator-loss class the PRD's own gotcha cites (patterns.md:522, renderHelp losing the space at 24 chars): the implementer applied that check to `stats --help` but not to their own new table. The sibling `renderTokensTable` never hit it because `issueNumber.padEnd(14)` only ever holds short ids like `CAM-470`. Fix mechanically in one file: truncate (or ellipsize) cycleId to CYCLE_COL_WIDTH - 1, or widen the column past the observed max and add a guaranteed separator.

userStories.notes: Files: NEW src/stats/cycles.ts, NEW test/commands/stats-cycles.test.ts. Shape precedent to copy closely: src/stats/tokens.ts (pure string-in/data-out module, tolerant parseLine/asDetailRecord helpers, accumulator + collect projection). Slice rule (ADR-0053, read it before coding): a slice runs from the event AFTER the previous cycle-tokens marker THROUGH the current marker; the first marker has no established left bound and publishes NO row; the leading span is disclosed as the header's unattributedLeadingEvents count, exactly mirroring how unattributedTokens is kept as a distinct field (src/stats/tokens.ts:44-61) and always printed (src/commands/stats.ts:93-103). Row fields: cycleId, issueNumber, closedAt (the marker's recordedAt), workerRounds (count of worker-start events in the slice), reviewRounds (DISTINCT detail.round values), plus the marker's token figures used exactly as recorded (CycleTokensEventDetail, src/supervisor/events.ts:421-431), plus prNumber and mergeMode ONLY for slices containing a 'shipped' ship-phase-result. Field names workerRounds and reviewRounds are load-bearing: US-002's value oracles select them by name via jq. GOTCHAS: (a) review-verdict-handback has two emit sites (src/supervisor/loop.ts:1890 MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT promotion and :1926 normal handback), so one round can emit two events; 9 of 269 real slices carry duplicate rounds, worst case cam/pr-204-plan-block-replan-loop with 5 events over rounds [1,2]. (c) cycleId is an OPAQUE free-form string (branch names, DRAIN-*, bare CAM-N, SESSION-*, SPEC-*, operator-ceremony-*): never parse it, never derive a date from it, never sort by it. (d) noUncheckedIndexedAccess: every array/regex-group access is T|undefined, guard it. (e) The header must stay deterministic (no generatedAt) or US-003's byte-identical-rebuild requirement becomes unsatisfiable. Test quality: hit real fixtures built in the test file plus at least one assertion against the repo's own log content read from disk if convenient, and never assert only that a mock was called.

`/* c8 ignore next */` is still present and is still the only c8/istanbul pragma in the repo (round-1 SUGGESTION, unaddressed). Coverage runs on bun's built-in reporter via `bun run check:coverage`, which does not honour it, so the pragma is inert and implies tooling the project does not use. The defensive throw itself is correct; prefer a plain comment stating the invariant.

`mergeMode as MergeMode` still widens an arbitrary string to the `'immediate' | 'ci-gated'` union after only a `typeof === 'string'` check (round-1 SUGGESTION, unaddressed). The tolerant-reader posture is right, but US-002 AC8 forbids publishing a bogus mergeMode and a membership test (`mergeMode === 'immediate' || mergeMode === 'ci-gated'`) would enforce it in the type system rather than trusting the emit site. Same cost, strictly stronger guarantee. The AC8 oracle passes on today's real log, so this is latent rather than live.

`parseStatsArgs` computes `rebuild: args.slice(1).includes('--rebuild')` and silently ignores every other token, so a typo (`cam stats cycles --rebiuld`) produces output byte-identical to a successful read-only run with no signal that the artifact was not regenerated (round-1 SUGGESTION, unaddressed). This mirrors the in-file `parseJournalArgs` precedent for `--force`/`--cycle-close`, so it is not a convention break, but unlike those booleans a dropped `--rebuild` is completely silent. Consider rejecting unknown flags after the subcommand as `parseRunArgs` already does.

`--rebuild` writes `scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl` into the working tree at any cwd with no branch guard, while the PRD's own posture (US-002/US-004 notes, the CAM-121 clobber scar) is that no feature branch may ever commit this file again after this PR (round-1 SUGGESTION, unaddressed). Neither the code nor STATS_HELP states that. Consider a warning (or hard refusal) when `--rebuild` runs off main, or at minimum a line in the STATS_HELP Behaviour body.

`readCycleMetricsContentFromMain` hardcodes the string literal `'main:scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl'` while the write path uses the `CYCLE_METRICS_JSONL_PATH` constant defined 13 lines above, so the path now lives in two places. The literal is oracle-driven (US-003 AC2 greps for exactly that byte sequence, which a template literal `main:${CYCLE_METRICS_JSONL_PATH}` would not satisfy), so this is understandable rather than careless; noting it only so a future path change is known to need both sites.

The README `## Commands` block lists `cam journal append` and `cam patterns archive` but still has no `cam stats` entry at all. This is pre-existing (`stats tokens` is missing too, so the new subcommand does not create a fresh inconsistency) and no acceptance criterion requires it, but this PR is the natural point to add a `cam stats tokens|cycles` line to the block.
